title: Hotpath micro-sampler with circuit-breaker backpressure to cut tracing allocations
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Our in-process tracer contributes non-trivial allocations and mutex contention on the request hotpath during high QPS (observed up to 6% p50 CPU increase and 8% p99 latency tail on small inference requests). Current tail-based and reservoir samplers make decisions late and sometimes allocate full span objects even for discarded traces. Goal: introduce a minimal-cost micro-sampler that makes an early low-cost decision, defers expensive span instantiation, and uses a circuit-breaker backpressure signal to avoid overwhelming downstream samplers or writers during bursts. Approach: 1) Add a <=8-byte inline sampling token (probabilistic) at ingress to decide keep/discard with per-route configurable rate. 2) If token indicates 'maybe', attach a lightweight trace-handle (no span allocations) that records only low-cost counters and a tiny decision score. 3) Integrate a small adaptive circuit-breaker that flips to 'throttle' mode when the tracing pipeline or downstream writer queue depth exceeds thresholds; when throttled, all 'maybe' decisions become no-op. 4) Late promotion: background worker periodically evaluates handles against tail heuristics and promotes a small percentage for full span materialization. 5) Provide a per-tenant burst budget and decay window to reduce thrash. Trade-offs: slight probability of missing some spans that would have been useful for debugging; additional complexity in tracer state machine. Mitigations: canary rollout, aggressive observability, and ability to pin sampling to 100% for customers with debugging needs. Design artifacts: design doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qZ-TRACER-micro-sampler, proposal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4587. Metrics to track: tracer CPU, allocation rate, span allocation count, writer queue depth, sample keep rate, p50/p95/p99 latency by route, error rate delta. Acceptance criteria: - end-to-end hotpath allocations reduced by >=40% in canary workloads - tracer-related mutex waits reduced by >=50% - no customer-visible increase in error-rate or p99 tail for non-traced requests - observability dashboards updated and alerting for writer-backpressure thresholds

If span allocation delta < -30% and no error-rate regression, increase to 25% for 12 hours
